[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Networking Fundamentals and OSI Model in Cyber Security"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding networking fundamentals and the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model is foundational for cyber security professionals. Security analysts, penetration testers, and network architects rely on this framework to diagnose vulnerabilities, analyze network traffic, and design robust defenses."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to the OSI Model"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The OSI model is a conceptual framework that standardizes the functions of a telecommunication or computing system without regard to its underlying internal structure and technology. It divides network communication into seven distinct layers, moving from physical hardware up to software applications."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 7: Application - Provides network services to end-user applications (e.g., HTTP, FTP, SMTP)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 6: Presentation - Translates, encrypts, and compresses data for the application layer."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 5: Session - Manages sessions between applications (establishment, maintenance, and termination)."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 4: Transport - Ensures reliable data transfer, flow control, and error correction (e.g., TCP, UDP)."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 3: Network - Handles routing, forwarding, and logical addressing (e.g., IP, ICMP)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 2: Data Link - Provides node-to-node data transfer and physical addressing using MAC addresses (e.g., Ethernet, Switches)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 1: Physical - Transmits raw bit streams over physical media (e.g., Cables, Hubs, Radio frequencies)."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Relevance to Cyber Security"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"In security, attacks and defenses map directly to these OSI layers. By understanding where an attack occurs, security tools can be deployed at the corresponding layer for mitigation."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 2 Attacks: ARP Spoofing, MAC Flooding. Defenses include Port Security and Dynamic ARP Inspection."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 3 Attacks: IP Spoofing, ICMP Floods. Defenses include Access Control Lists (ACLs) and Firewalls."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 4 Attacks: SYN Floods, Port Scanning. Defenses include Stateful Firewalls and SYN Cookies."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer 7 Attacks: SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), HTTP Flood. Defenses include Web Application Firewalls (WAF) and Input Validation."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Practical Traffic Analysis with Scapy"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Security analysts frequently interact with network packets using Python and Scapy to understand protocol behavior and inspect headers across different OSI layers."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"from scapy.all import IP, TCP, sr1

# Constructing a Layer 3 (IP) and Layer 4 (TCP) packet
packet = IP(dst="192.168.1.1") / TCP(dport=80, flags="S")

# Sending the packet and receiving the response
response = sr1(packet, timeout=2, verbose=False)

if response:
    print("Received response from target")
    response.show()
else:
    print("No response received")"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering networking fundamentals and the OSI model allows security professionals to dissect malicious traffic, perform effective incident response, and implement layered security architectures (defense-in-depth) to protect organizational assets."}]
